findings.title: Fix test cleanup so it removes the IDPs the test created
Invalidate login IDP cache when organization state changes, not only on IDP updates
Check other callers of the shared SPI `getLoginPredicate()` after the semantic change

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Test cleanup uses literal string 'alias' instead of the actual IDP alias, leaving 21 IDPs (idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20) not removed after the test, which can cause flaky tests
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the cleanup code uses the literal string 'alias' instead of the dynamically generated IDP alias names ('idp-alias-' + i or 'idp-alias-0' through 'idp-alias-20'). The golden comment points out the incorrect alias reference, and the candidate issue explains the same problem with additional context about the consequence (21 IDPs not being removed). They are describing the exact same bug.

false_positives.candidate: Login IDP cache is only invalidated on IDP create/update/remove but not when organization state changes (e.g., disabling an organization), causing stale cached IDP IDs
The isEnabled() re-check was only added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, so other callers of getForLogin may get IDPs belonging to disabled organizations

getLoginPredicate() semantic change now requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true for org-linked IDPs, which affects all existing consumers of this public SPI helper and may silently exclude non-public org IDPs in unintended contexts

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
